steps.title: A repertoire, and a new composition with three writers and two recordings
steps.say: An invented catalog: 400 works, 586 recordings, 111 parties, 3,140 claims by territory and window, label contracts with advances, and a landmark fingerprint for every recording's synthetic audio. Then a registration: a composition with three writers whose shares must sum to one and a publisher; two recordings of it on one label, one with its audio fingerprinted. The rights graph shows the claims the registration created and that every right sums to one.

steps.title: A quarter of usage files, with the usual damage
steps.say: 3,065 lines from two streaming services and a broadcaster: a little over half carry an ISRC, the rest a title and artist with remaster suffixes, 'feat.' credits, dropped letters, upper case, surname-first artists and 'The' moved to the end; 40 lines are reported twice and one recording has a one-day spike in Germany. Each line is resolved to a recording with a confidence; the confident ones are matched, the middling held for review, the duplicates flagged, and the spike named.

steps.title: An audio clip matched to the right recording
steps.say: Eight seconds cut from the middle of one catalog recording's synthetic audio with noise added: spectrogram peaks paired across notes into hashes, votes on recording and time offset. The best match, its offset into the recording, and how far it beats the runner-up. The method and the audio are both labelled for what they are.

steps.title: Royalties by territory and contract window
steps.say: Every matched line in the quarter: the gross split into pools by source (streaming 52% master, 6.5% mechanical, 6.5% performance; broadcast 22% performance), each pool split by the claims in force for that territory and date, worldwide claims yielding to territorial carve-outs. Label contracts take the artist's share and recoup the advance first. Anything with no claim in force is unclaimed; anything whose claims do not sum to one is held.

steps.title: An overlapping claim, and the money moves to hold
steps.say: A second publisher registers a 50% performance claim in Germany on North Stone, a work already fully claimed worldwide. The consistency check finds Germany summing to 150%, a dispute opens with the evidence, and the next calculation holds that work's German performance money instead of paying it. The rights graph and the writer's statement show the hold. Nothing is resolved by the system; a person closes the dispute.

steps.title: The audit trail
steps.say: Who loaded, registered, imported, matched, calculated and claimed, in a hash chain: the trail the blueprint asks for behind every unmatched line and every conflicting claim.
